generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL; never overwritten by boundary pools; when appending to a compact database, start after the maximum existing key. For composite PKs, generate the first component sequentially and the remaining components sequentially per first component (e.g. draft_number 0,1,2,... per document_id; copy_number 1,2,3,... per (document_id,draft_number)).
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy an existing parent key value; allow NULL only where the column is nullable; include at least one parent row with no children; never emit dangling child FKs; never mutate FK columns after linkage is built. For composite FKs, sample whole parent tuples jointly (not per-column) so the composite tuple exists in the parent.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer in [1, 100] unless a per-column exception gives a tighter range; include boundary values at listed literals and one step on each side.
generic_sampling_rules.char_code: Pick from the enum pool of the referenced reference table; preserve exact case; include near-variants (lower/upper case) only where a per-column exception lists them. For enum-constrained columns, restrict sampling to the enum pool (plus NULL where nullable) and disable random string mutation.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_text: Short lowercase alphabetic token of length 1-3 from string.ascii_lowercase; allow near-duplicate values and case variants where a per-column exception lists them; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Random datetime between 1970-01-01 and 2016-12-31, format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, at least one NULL row per instance; share follows the compact database share (0.0 observed, so use a small share such as 1 row per instance); apply after all row filtering and after all hint application so at least one NULL survives; verify at least one NULL and one non-NULL per nullable column before writing.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_and_tie: For columns listed in per_column_exceptions with pattern comparison_boundary, guarantee at least one occurrence of each listed literal (and one step on each side where numeric) in the generated rows for the targeted non-key columns; for ties_for_order_limit include at least two rows sharing the listed rank value; for duplicates_for_distinct include 20-50% duplicate values; apply only to non-key columns or re-derive child FKs from the final parent key set afterwards.
generic_sampling_rules.table_size_jitter: Table sizes are base + 0/1 jitter upward so children can leave parents unreferenced; the base values are given in table_sizes_per_instance.

supporting_evidence.enum_rules: Ref_Document_Status, Ref_Document_Types, Ref_Shipping_Agents, Roles rows show the listed code pools; Documents and Employees draw from them.
supporting_evidence.range_rules: All PK and FK integer columns are positive in the shown rows; draft_number includes 0 (Document_Drafts row document_id=1, draft_number=0).
supporting_evidence.no_formulas: No calculated column is present in the schema; no offset or rate can be derived from the shown rows.
supporting_evidence.fk_integrity: All child FK values in the shown rows match existing parent keys; no dangling FKs are observed, so unmatched_join_rows is realized via parent-without-child only.
supporting_evidence.pk_uniqueness: Ref_Document_Types.document_type_code, Ref_Document_Status.document_status_code, Roles.role_code and Ref_Shipping_Agents.shipping_agent_code are PRIMARY KEY columns and cannot contain duplicates; duplicates_for_distinct is therefore restricted to non-key columns.
supporting_evidence.composite_keys: Document_Drafts, Draft_Copies and Circulation_History have composite PKs; the non-first components must be generated sequentially per first component and composite FKs must be sampled as whole tuples.
supporting_evidence.group_size_feasibility: Circulation_History size is raised to 6 so that group sizes 1, 2 and >=3 can be realized for its grouping columns.

uncertainty: Observed NULL rates are 0.0 for all nullable columns; a minimal NULL share (one row per nullable column per instance) is used to exercise NULL semantics. No date-pair order rule exists because no table has two related dates. No formula is stated because no column is derived from other columns in the shown rows. Group-size and tie patterns on PK/FK columns are realized through child-row counts rather than key mutation, so they may not be forced in every instance. Case-variant boundary literals on enum-constrained columns are predicate-only and are not materialized as values.
